text:
alex: Hey team — we have a customer on node20 + redwood-js-sdk@1.2.7 seeing duplicate POSTs when a request times out and the SDK retries. Billing shows two create calls.

maya: ugh, can you paste the trace ids / logs?

alex: logs show original request id req_01a then retry req_01b ~200ms later. server received two POST /v1/ops with same payload.

alex: minimal log snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T14:12:01.123Z] req=req_01a status=499 aborted by client signal
[2026-03-14T14:12:01.330Z] sdk retry attempt=1 req=req_01b method=POST path=/v1/ops status=200 id=resp_9001
```

alex: env: node v20.4.0, npm ls undici -> undici@5.13.0, globalThis.fetch is node's built-in, but user polyfilled undici in other codepaths.

support-bot: Support ticket #45712 created and attached. Adding @eric from infra.

eric: thanks. two quick suspects: 1) body is a streaming Readable (not re-readable) and SDK retries send same stream again; 2) AbortController handoff semantics changed in node20 fetch/undici combo.

maya: can you share a tiny repro? even a 10-line script helps.

alex: here is the customer's repro (sanitized):
```
const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-js-sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retry: { maxAttempts: 2, backoffMs: 100 } });

// streaming body coming from file
const fs = require('fs');
const stream = fs.createReadStream('./payload.json');

const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 50); // abort early to trigger retry

await client.request('/v1/ops', { method: 'POST', body: stream, signal: ac.signal });
```

alex: when aborted, SDK issues a retry but passes the same Readable stream instance — node's streams aren't rewindable so the second request ends up getting re-sent from the underlying OS socket or sometimes empty body depending on timing.

eric: that matches. We never clone stream bodies. For JSON streams the safe approach is to buffer or require string/Buffer bodies for retries.

eng-oncall: quick mitigation for customer — set retry.maxAttempts=0 or switch body to a string via fs.readFileSync and JSON.parse+stringify to avoid streaming. Also add an idempotency header on server side to dedupe.

pm-jen: customer is on hosted billing and worried about duplicate charges. We should provide them a patch ASAP and a recommended short-term config change.

eric: I pushed a branch that detects non-rewindable bodies and will opt out of automatic retries unless the user opts into body buffering. Proposed SDK change: if body is a ReadableStream, log a warning and skip retries unless retry.forceBuffer=true. Also add docs.

maya: can we detect when AbortController is used and ensure not to reuse the same controller across retry paths? Some user code reuses controller across requests which causes signal already aborted on retry.

eric: good call. Current bug surface: (a) reusing AbortController across request lifecycle, (b) stream bodies not cloneable, (c) undici/node20 fetch semantics differ when globalThis.fetch is polyfilled. Steps to repro locally:
```
npm i redwood-js-sdk@1.2.7 undici@5 && node repro.js
node -v
npm ls undici
```

alex: customer confirmed they polyfilled undici earlier in app code (so two different fetch implementations in process). That can cause double sends if SDK uses undici.request under the hood but runtime fetch uses node's fetch.

eng-oncall: recommended customer steps we gave: 1) set retry.maxAttempts=0 or 0->1; 2) switch to non-streaming body (JSON string) for critical endpoints; 3) add Idempotency-Key header (uuid) server-side dedupe; 4) run npm ls undici and ensure single fetch shim.

eric: long term: SDK patch will (1) detect stream bodies and avoid silent retries, (2) clone small bodies into memory up to 1MB, (3) emit a clear warning when global fetch and undici mismatch detected, (4) add a helper retry-safe send that buffers body. Targeting 1.2.8 release.

pm-jen: please include a short KB we can send to customers explaining the billing exposure and safe configs.

alex: customer applied workaround (stringify body + idempotency header) and confirmed no duplicates after 24h. They've accepted temporary mitigation.

maya: tracking: support ticket #45712 -> escalated to eng, patch planned for 1.2.8, docs PR, KB note.

support-bot: Note: follow-up scheduled in 48h. :calendar: 

alex: thx everyone, leaving logs + repro in the ticket.
